issue.title: Remove stale Symvision epic-symbol exemptions for closed bead sase-nb
issue.description: just check fails at the lint (symvision) gate on a clean master tree (HEAD dc221a458, verified with 'git stash -u' so no local diff was present). Every earlier gate passes (fmt python/markdown, keep-sorted, ruff, mypy, feature flags, pyscripts, test waits, changelog, patch/stitch terminology); symvision then rejects five Justfile --epic-symbol entries because epic bead sase-nb closed at 2026-08-17T02:21:31Z: sase-nb(encode_feature_flags_env), sase-nb(feature_flags_schema_block), sase-nb(feature_flags_schema_drift), sase-nb(FlagDueStyle), and sase-nb(reset_process_feature_flags) — Justfile lines 321-324 and 330 inside the _lint-symvision recipe. Error text per entry: "bead 'sase-nb' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol." Reproduction: 'just install && just check' (or 'just _lint-symvision' alone) on master. Impact: every agent whose tree reaches this gate is blocked by a stale whitelist unrelated to their diff. Scope: remove the five stale Justfile exemptions and clean up the underlying feature-flag symbols per the Symvision epic-whitelist policy (each is now either genuinely used, or should be privatized/deleted); leave the still-open sase-n4 and sase-n4.5 entries alone.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-nm — same stale Symvision --epic-symbol pattern for a closed bead (sase-n9), closed as done once those Justfile entries and symbols were cleaned up; useful precedent for the fix shape, not a duplicate of these sase-nb symbols.

RELATED: sase-kc — the same recurring pattern for closed bead sase-js; three instances in a week (sase-jg, sase-kc, sase-nm) suggest the epic land step should drop its own --epic-symbol entries at close time.

ALREADY FIXED — this task can be closed as done (or as a duplicate of the fix) without any further work.

All five stale entries this bead names were removed by commit ec2cc1912 'refactor(flags): retire the sase-nb epic-symbol whitelist', authored by the sase-nb.11 land agent at 2026-08-16T22:36:25-04:00 — 46 seconds after this bead was created at 22:35:39 EDT, so the two agents raced on the same gate rather than finding two problems. The Justfile diff drops exactly sase-nb(encode_feature_flags_env), sase-nb(feature_flags_schema_block), sase-nb(feature_flags_schema_drift), sase-nb(FlagDueStyle), and sase-nb(reset_process_feature_flags), and leaves the still-open sase-n4 and sase-n4.5 entries untouched, as this bead's scope asked.

Each symbol was resolved on its own merits rather than re-whitelisted, per the Symvision epic-whitelist policy: feature_flags_schema_block and feature_flags_schema_drift got the existing tools/ pragma (their real consumers are tools/sync_feature_flags_schema and tools/check_feature_flags, which Symvision does not scan); encode_feature_flags_env and FlagDueStyle were privatized and dropped from __all__; reset_process_feature_flags was deleted from src/sase/feature_flags/snapshot.py and its seam moved into tests/_conftest_runtime.py.

VERIFIED: a monitored 'just check-full' on ec2cc1912 (2026-08-17T02:38-02:51Z) reports 'lint (symvision)' green along with every other lint gate, and the full non-visual pytest lane passed (31843 passed, 11 skipped). That run's only failure is the pre-existing suite-cost budget gate tracked by sase-j0.

The recurring-pattern observation in this bead's second RELATED note (sase-jg, sase-kc, sase-nm — the epic land step should drop its own --epic-symbol entries at close) is a real and still-unaddressed improvement; it is worth keeping even though this specific instance is resolved.

CLOSED AS DONE — no work required (triage sweep 2026-08-17, workspace sase_12).

This bead was filed at 2026-08-17T02:35:39 EDT reporting that 'just check' fails at the symvision gate because five Justfile --epic-symbol entries name closed epic bead sase-nb. Commit ec2cc1912 'refactor(flags): retire the sase-nb epic-symbol whitelist' landed 46 seconds later at 22:36:25-04:00, authored by the sase-nb.11 land agent: the two agents raced on the same gate rather than finding two problems.

VERIFIED ON CURRENT MASTER cf7eeee03: 'grep -n epic-symbol Justfile' returns only sase-n4.5(ProviderDisableWriteOutcome) and six sase-n4(...) entries, all for beads that are still in progress. None of the five sase-nb symbols this bead names — encode_feature_flags_env, feature_flags_schema_block, feature_flags_schema_drift, FlagDueStyle, reset_process_feature_flags — remains in the file.

Each symbol was resolved on its merits rather than re-whitelisted, per the Symvision epic-whitelist policy: the two schema symbols took the existing tools/ pragma, encode_feature_flags_env and FlagDueStyle were privatized and dropped from __all__, and reset_process_feature_flags was deleted with its seam moved into tests/_conftest_runtime.py.

NOT CLOSED WITH THIS BEAD: its second RELATED note observes that this is the fourth instance of the same pattern in a week (sase-jg, sase-kc, sase-nm, and this one) and proposes that the epic land step drop its own --epic-symbol entries at close time. That improvement is real and still unaddressed; it is routed separately through /sase_new_task rather than dying with this bead.
